what_it_did.what_the_split_means: A mechanical commit republishes an unchanged net -- the report, the dashboard, the state files. Counting those as work would make a quiet day look busy, so they are separated rather than filtered: they happened, they are just not progress.

what_it_decided.thesis_read: For the first time the project's own question has been asked on the right book and answered out loud. The I&C suspension the director ruled on 24 August landed (`4e884cdbf`), the comparison was re-run on the book it creates, and the answer is written where he can read it: on resi + SME the value arm earns net GBP 96,461.44 against the frozen flat-rules control's GBP 79,688.17 -- +GBP 16,773.28, +21.0% -- and on households alone +GBP 11,828.26. Per-customer pricing beats flat rules on this supplier's residential book. That is the sentence three orientations could not say, and I want to be exact about how much it is worth, because the artefact is more honest about itself than a headline would be. It is thin in three ways that all point at the same thing. `concentration_top_n_share_of_absolute_movement` is 0.9941 -- of 211 accounts compared, 60 moved and 15 are 99.4% of all movement, every one of them a SEED account; the ~200 the funnel grew are rounding errors. Of the 42 renewals the arm priced, 20 ended at the ceiling and none at the floor, at a median chosen margin of GBP 57.75/MWh against the control's GBP 2.00 -- so roughly half the arm's answers were decided by where the grid was cut, not by anything it inferred about the customer, and GBP 57.75 is seven to fifteen times the EBIT allowance Ofgem grants an efficient supplier. And gross margin FELL by GBP 14,151.51 while net ROSE by GBP 16,773.28, a GBP 30,924 divergence of which lower bad debt explains GBP 2,591.09; the artefact records that as observed and unexplained (R9) and says plainly that until it is attributed, the mechanism behind the win is not established. Against the thesis -- advantage from INFERENCE, never ACCESS -- what has been shown is that the arm beats flat rules on about seven households and two small businesses, by a mechanism nobody has yet named. Then the ground moved again 3.4 hours later and by our own hand: `fb8a8fda5` made the funnel win gas legs, the book went 226 -> 419 accounts and 91.5% dual fuel, and every account inside that A/B's window is single-fuel. The reading is correct for its book and its book is already superseded. On the inference axis specifically the news is worse and it is mine: EP1 was named in focus for the second time and drawn, and the estimator did not change. `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability` is still `min(0.05 + 0.03 * bill_shock_count, cap)`, and `coupled_gap_ledger.json` still reports `distinct_hazards: 1`, `hazard_histogram {"0.05": 33}` and a believed tenure of 20.0 years for every graded account. The company still has no per-customer view of lifetime on the only population it now serves. What went right beyond the measurement is the disease itself: tree divergence fell from 436 files to 31, origin went from 46 heads to 1 with every deleted branch's tip recorded first in `BRANCH_DISPOSITION_2026-08-26.md`, and the checker crash that had refused every staging commit for six days was fixed, clearing a 419-file archive backlog. And the steering mechanism worked -- last orientation four of five focus items were unreachable by any draw; this time three of four landed and the fourth was drawn. The direction is now reaching the work. What it is pointing at is still half-measured.

focus.what: Re-run `python3 -m tools.run_value_cycle_ab` on the book as it now stands and, in the SAME reading, attribute the gross-fell-while-net-rose divergence. Both are owed in the artefact's own words: `docs/design/THE_VALUE_CYCLE_REALISED_AB.md` carries a note saying its current figures predate `fb8a8fda5` and are owed a re-run, and its closing section names attributing the divergence as "the next step, ahead of any further mechanism repair". The book changed materially, not cosmetically -- 226 to 419 accounts, 222 electricity and 197 gas, 91.5% of won homes now dual fuel, `TOTAL_GAS_AQ` 1,959,100 kWh -- and one household is one billing account via `saas.customer_reaction._billing_account_id`, so cost-to-serve, churn and lifetime value all move. The divergence to attribute is precise: control gross GBP 433,174.76 against arm GBP 419,023.25 (-GBP 14,151.51) while net went +GBP 16,773.28, a GBP 30,924 gap of which bad debt explains GBP 2,591.09. `total_gross` is revenue minus wholesale; `total_net` is after levies, network, capital and bad debt -- so decompose the difference line by line from the run's own ledger rather than from the summary, and check the two extra churned accounts (32 -> 34) as a volume explanation rather than asserting it. The candidate explanations are currently recorded as inferred and must not be promoted to measured without the arithmetic. Rewrite the artefact's headline table so the current row names its book -- dual fuel, account count, commit -- and keep the superseded rows and their supersession notes; nothing here is rewritten. R14: every figure carries its clock.
focus.why: This is the only number in the project that answers the director's question, and right now it is correct about a book the company no longer has, for the second time in three days. That is the failure mode this whole stretch was spent escaping, and it recurred inside twelve hours by our own hand rather than by neglect. The attribution matters more than the re-run: an arm charging a median GBP 57.75/MWh against GBP 2.00 that ends the run with LESS gross margin is not obviously winning by pricing at all, and until the GBP 30,924 is attributed, "+GBP 16,773" is a result without a mechanism -- which is exactly the shape that let a GBP 3.08M figure stand for two days as a fact about five accounts. It is first because items two and three are both measured by this instrument and neither can be read until it names its own book. Finished when the artefact's current row states the dual-fuel book and its account count, the delta is re-reported whichever way it moved -- including smaller, or negative, said plainly -- and the gross-versus-net divergence is either decomposed into named cost lines with figures, or recorded as still unexplained WITH the candidates that were tested and ruled out. Do not soften a fall: the director's standing instruction is that a negative result on the right population is worth more than a headline on the wrong one.

focus.what: Give the tenure horizon per-account dispersion from observables the company can actually know. Named for the third time and unchanged since the second, so the instruction is the same and the diagnosis is settled -- do not re-derive it. `coupled_gap_ledger.json` `components.lifetime_level`: `distinct_hazards: 1`, `hazard_histogram {"0.05": 33}`, `hazard_is_constant_across_graded_population: true`, median believed tenure 20.0 years for every graded account, measured 11:46:22Z. Cause: `saas/churn_model.py::churn_probability` is `min(0.05 + 0.03 * bill_shock_count, cap)`, a step function of one integer that is zero for 42% of renewal decisions, consumed by `company/analytics/clv_three_horizon.py` at H2 as `hazard = latest.churn_probability` with the term `1.0 / hazard`. The LEVEL is about right -- `hazard_calibration` reads 0.05 believed against 0.053 realised over 263 decisions -- so this is dispersion, not calibration, and nothing may be tuned toward a smaller gap (R12); the 0.204 scalar is not to be applied. Widen the propensity to use what a supplier observes about a household: payment method and payment behaviour, tenure to date, the account's own tariff against the market it could switch to, consumption volatility, contact and complaint history -- and now, because it exists as of `fb8a8fda5`, whether the account carries a gas leg, which the director named as a driver of churn and lifetime value in the same breath as cost-to-serve. Check every input against the wall before using it: if it needs a simulation internal it is a violation, and `company/interfaces/sim_interface.py` is the only door. Re-measure with `python3 -m tools.couple_clv` and report the ledger's next reading whichever way it moves; a level move to 3 is available on this evidence if the coupled rung is genuinely met -- self- certify with `record_level_up_self_certified`, never `--no-verify` a `level_current` change.
focus.why: The thesis names inference and this is the axis it is named after: a supplier deciding customer-by-customer on LIFETIME VALUE, whose lifetime term takes exactly one value across every graded account, is not deciding per customer on lifetime at all. Item one will now report a win or a loss on households, and either way the reading is unattributable while this term is a constant -- the arm's advantage, whatever its sign, cannot be coming from a belief that does not vary. The contrast is already published and sharpens the point: `belief_vs_outcome. discrimination_auc` is 0.6944 on 24 matched decisions, so the RETENTION belief the arm prices with does carry information about who stays, while the LIFETIME belief carries none. It is second rather than first only because item one is a few hours and gates the reading everything else is judged by. Finished when the graded population shows more than one distinct hazard, the ledger's next entry comes from a changed estimator rather than a changed sample, every new input is named with the observable it comes from and cleared against the wall, and the new gap is recorded whichever direction it went. If it worsens, that is the result and saying so is the deliverable.

focus.what: Establish why the value arm's maximiser still runs to its own bound on half the book, and either make the optimum interior for a reason that is about the customer, or report in the A/B artefact that the arm's win is a bound's and not an inference's. The measurement is in `docs/observability/value_cycle_ab_resi.json` `decision_shape`: 42 priced, 8 declined, `endpoint_at_ceiling` 20, `endpoint_at_floor` 0, `ceiling_bound` 20, `extrapolation_bound` 2, `median_margin_gbp_per_mwh` 57.75 against a control of 2.00. Start from the already-filed diagnosis rather than a fresh one: `docs/staging/WORKER_FINDING_THE_CHURN_MODELS_CAP_MAKES_THE_PROFIT_MAXIMISING_PRICE_UNBOUNDED_2026-08-25.md` names the root cause as `company/crm/churn_model.py::estimate_churn_probability` calibrating its rate sensitivity on GB MARKET-WIDE switching, which is the wrong curve for a single supplier moving its own price while the market does not -- and records that the two captive floors are already gone and interior optima exist on 255 of 263 accounts, which the A/B's 20 of 42 appears to contradict. Reconcile those two figures first: they are measured on different populations and one of them is describing a book the company no longer serves. Any change to the sensitivity is a fidelity change and must cite a published source (Ofgem switching data, an academic or regulatory elasticity estimate), never a chosen number, and must be decided blind to what it does to the arm's result (R13, R12). If the honest answer is that no defensible curve makes the optimum interior, say that in the artefact instead of moving the ceiling.
focus.why: This is the thesis test stated as arithmetic. "The advantage must come from INFERENCE, never ACCESS" fails just as completely when the advantage comes from a BOUND -- a price set by the lawful/competitive ceiling is a price the arm did not choose, and roughly half of its priced answers are that. It also runs straight into the director's standing priority, which is credibility rather than profit: "every customer and segment is individually credible and free of inconsistencies ... a household that couldn't exist is not." A household on a GBP 57.75/MWh retail margin -- seven to fifteen times the GBP 3.73-8.54/MWh EBIT allowance Ofgem grants an efficient supplier -- is close to that line, and this is the arm we would eventually wire to the renewal desk. It is third because item one determines whether these particular numbers survive the dual-fuel book and item two is the belief the arm reasons from; it is on the list because without it a positive A/B cannot be attributed to inference no matter how many times it is re-run. Finished when the 20-of-42 and the 255-of-263 are reconciled with their populations named, and either the arm's answers are interior for a sourced reason or the artefact states in its own headline section that the bound decided.
